Methods for nbreg fits

Source: R/methods-nbreg.R
nbreg-methods.Rd

Standard extractor and summary methods for objects returned by nbreg().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.nbreg'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
residuals(object, type = c("pearson", "response"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbreg'
predict(object, newdata, type = c("response", "link"), offset = NULL, ...)

Arguments

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

...

Not used.

object, x

An object of class "nbreg" (or "summary.nbreg" for the print method of a summary).

type

For residuals(): "pearson" (default), \((y_i - \hat\mu_i)/\sqrt{\hat\mu_i + \hat\mu_i^2/\hat\theta}\), or "response", \(y_i - \hat\mu_i\). For predict(): "response" (default) for \(\hat\mu\), or "link" for the linear predictor \(\hat\eta = \log\hat\mu\).

newdata

Optional data frame for predict(). If omitted, predictions are for the data used in the fit.

offset

For predict() with newdata: an optional offset vector (in addition to any offset() term in the formula).

Value

coef() the coefficient vector; vcov() its covariance matrix; logLik() an object of class "logLik" with df = number of coefficients + 1 (for \(\theta\)) and nobs; fitted() the fitted means; residuals() a residual vector; nobs() the number of observations; predict() a vector of predictions; summary() an object of class "summary.nbreg" containing the coefficient table.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(300))
d$y <- rnbinom(300, size = 2, mu = exp(0.5 + 0.8 * d$x))
fit <- nbreg(y ~ x, data = d)
fit
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = y ~ x, data = d)
#> 
#> Negative binomial (NB2) regression, log link, fitted by IRLS + Newton-Raphson
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#> (Intercept)            x  
#>      0.4508       0.7669  
#> 
#> Theta: 1.95   Log-likelihood: -526.892 on 3 df
summary(fit)
#> 
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = y ~ x, data = d)
#> 
#> Pearson residuals:
#>     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
#> -1.1939 -0.7791 -0.2593  0.4389  5.2098 
#> 
#> Coefficients (negative binomial with log link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
#> (Intercept)  0.45081    0.06613   6.817 9.32e-12 ***
#> x            0.76687    0.06699  11.448  < 2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> 
#> Theta: 1.95  (SE 0.3699)
#> Log-likelihood: -526.892 on 3 df   AIC: 1059.78   BIC: 1070.89
#> Outer iterations (IRLS + Newton-Raphson): 3
coef(fit)
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   0.4508058   0.7668655 
AIC(fit)
#> [1] 1059.783
head(residuals(fit, type = "pearson"))
#>          1          2          3          4          5          6 
#> -0.8050751  2.2472901 -0.7620322  1.2691926 -0.5032198  0.1494196 
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(x = c(-1, 0, 1)))
#>        1        2        3 
#> 0.729016 1.569576 3.379309
